chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu Al-Rabie, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The one who drinks wine after Allah prohibited it upon my tongue is not worthy to be married when he proposes (have his proposal) accepted for marriage when he proposes.'
ai.seo_question: What is the marital status or eligibility of a person who drinks wine according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the juristic principle of *ghayr al-ahl* (unworthiness) for a *khamr* drinker, linking habitual consumption to a defect in marital suitability. It reflects the Shia scholarly view that while drinking wine is a major sin, it also serves as a disqualifying factor for marriage proposals due to the loss of dignity and moral integrity. The ruling underscores the connection between spiritual purity and social standing in Islamic family law.
